content: Onychia refers to an inflammatory condition affecting the nail matrix, which is the tissue surrounding the nail. This condition is characterized by the accumulation of pus and, in some cases, the detachment or shedding of the nail. The pathophysiology of onychia involves the entry of microscopic pathogens, such as bacteria or fungi, into the nail matrix through minor wounds or breaches in the skin barrier. One of the most common causes of onychia is the use of manicure tools that have not been adequately sterilized or disinfected, allowing the transmission of infectious agents.
